developments: Ranked for piece 01: (1) Proactive personal agents with account access have become mainstream consumer products. Meta's Muse, OpenAI's dots and Instinct shipped, Muse is promised for glasses, and Google folded Spark/tasks into the main Gemini chat. Hands-on tests (Vergecast, Jones, Mollick, Vo) show real wins alongside alarming purchase flows and data misfires. (2) Always-listening and camera wearables face a visible privacy reckoning. Meta shipped camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Amazon announced Bee Frontier/Eclipse, Norway proposed bans in public places, and the Vergecast argues listening itself, not only recording, is what unsettles people. (3) OS and home surfaces are being rebuilt around assistants: Windows hybrid intelligence (MXC shipped, Copilot actions promised), Googlebook's built-in Gemini, Apple HomeView's face-switched personal context, and Siri AI's beta. (4) Voice is earning narrow, real roles: Alexa Plus routines, Willison voice-coding while cooking, a phone call to dots, and Guided Vision and the Brera glasses pilot for accessibility. Research tempers this. Structured oversight beats chat for supervising GUI agents (TaskVM), delegation outpaces verification (Copilot study), direct manipulation still beats re-prompting for fine adjustments (Plottery), and spoken AI can shift opinions unnoticed.
missing_perspectives: Accessibility users speaking for themselves: Guided Vision and the Brera pilot rest only on vendor claims, with no blind or low-vision user testing. Non-US and non-English users are thin, limited to Norway's government, Meta's Italian pilot and dots' EEA unavailability, with no user experience. Users outside tech and older users appear only anecdotally (Cornell's mother, Muse being asked about by non-tech people). There are no privacy advocates or civil-society voices on Bee, Muse data training or glasses, and no bystanders. No one has hands-on with Windows Copilot actions or Autopilot beyond one commentator, because most are unshipped. Smart-glasses evidence is Meta-only, since Samsung and Nothing remain leaks. The Ray-Ban unprompted-recording bug is deferred because only relayed sources are available. There is no long-term or field study of computer-use agents with ordinary users.
balance: The accepted set has 39 items. Vendors supply 10 (Google 5, Meta 3, Microsoft 1, plus Meta's Brera pilot), each used for what shipped and for attributed claims. Independent journalism and reviews supply 13 (Vergecast 5, UploadVR 4, MKBHD 2, 9to5Google, Road to VR). Practitioners and commentators supply 12 (Willison, Mollick 2, NN/g 2, Witteveen 4, Nate B Jones 3, Claire Vo 2, Big Technology). Research supplies 4 arXiv preprints. Formats: written feeds, 7 podcasts and 7 videos all contribute. All three themes have usable evidence. Computer-use agents and personal context are heaviest. Voice is covered by Alexa Plus, Willison, Dots by phone, Live Avatar (vendor plus Witteveen), the voice-persuasion RCT, Plottery and Guided Vision. Each piece draws on well over three independent publishers. Several new items were deferred or rejected for relayed sourcing (Meta recording bug, FTC probe) or for being off-theme (XREAL, Chirp Pong). Universal Cart is held for a possible agentic-commerce thread.
